selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (access control applied)
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline showed no cron.allow/deny (open access); opsadmin user created; /etc/cron.allow written containing only root and opsadmin

selected_evidence.requirement: Verification that restriction is enforced (denied vs allowed users)
selected_evidence.summary: Before restriction, testuser1 and opsadmin could both install crontabs (exit 0). After applying /etc/cron.allow, testuser1's crontab install failed with 'not allowed to use this program' (exit 1) while opsadmin and root succeeded (exit 0)
Removed opsadmin/root test crontabs and deleted the temporary testuser1 account

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity on node1
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fa1e87e6-00f3-42d2-acc5-ad1df6c3d16a, cron.service active, /etc/cron.allow content confirmed prior to reboot
Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned acknowledgement (pid) before the node disconnected

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (actual restart, not just elapsed time)
selected_evidence.summary: Connection refused during reboot window, then node1 reachable again with new boot_id 4fd739f1-1bc9-41de-bc63-c54f8e7dc885, differing from pre-restart boot_id

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required config/service and data
selected_evidence.summary: cron.service active, /etc/cron.allow persisted intact with root and opsadmin, and opsadmin successfully scheduled and removed a cron job confirming functional access control after restart
